newsitem.title: UK: French,German stocks soar on benign U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: French,German stocks soar on benign U.S. data.

text.p: German and French stocks soared on Tuesday, boosted by U.S. economic data which showed reduced inflationary pressures and helped calm interest rate worries.
Frankfurt and Paris surged nearly two percent shortly after U.S. figures were released giving favourable figures on employment costs and durable goods. London was also nudged forward by the report.
Wall Street itself rapidly climbed 1.3 percent at the opening following the data. The sudden surge activated the New York Stock Exchange's limits on program trading.
"The (U.S.) data was definitely weaker than expected," said a London dealer. "People will be rethinking when the next U.S. interest rate move might be."

On currency markets, the weaker-than-expected data hit the dollar as the receding prospects of higher interest rates knocked the dollar off its recent high levels agains the mark and yen. It recovered slightly later.
French stocks were given the biggest lift by the data on reduced labour costs and a decline in durable goods orders, soaring 53.72 points to 2603.97 on the Paris CAC index at one point.
The impact was marked because the market had been on the look-out for signs of inflationary pressure. But trading was thin, perhaps because of lingering nerves over the upcoming French election.

In Frankfurt, shares spurted ahead, following in the path of government bonds after the Washington figures showed U.S. workers' compensation gains slowed in the first three months of 1997 as nearly flat benefit costs offset a sharp jump in wages.

Floor trade had ended before the Washington data, but transactions on the computerised IBIS index climbed 63.75 points to 3435.71 and breached a key resistance level at 3,400 points before slipping back slightly.
"Things are certainly positive in the very short term but I wouldn"t see this as real euphoria," cautioned one trader.

"With the public holiday just around the corner (May Day on Thursday) I can see some people flattening out their positions before too long. And there hasn't been enough of a broad sweep ahead to convince me," the trader added.
Banks and insurance companies, which often outperform when bond markets are strong because of the large fixed income portfolios they control, were among the leaders.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks jumped by 0.7 percent after a day of dull trading overshadowed by Thursday's British general election.
"The upward direction on Wall Street is certainly going to help us move ahead," said one dealer.
On currency markets, the dollar dropped as the Washington figures diminished the prospects of short-term rise in interest rates, which would hurt dollar-denominated assets.
The U.S. currency recovered somewhat when it found firm support at 1.7260 marks and edged back to the level seens in late European in London on Monday.
STOCKS AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 34.0 points at 4,423.7.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 48.74 points at 2,598.99.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed up 20.13 at 3,383.19.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7277 marks versus 1.7274 in late European trade on Monday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 126.80 from 126.61.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $339.25 after ending at $340.05 in London on Monday. Silver was at $4.65, down a cent.
